title: Second & Third Conditionals
subtitle: Imaginary situations now and in the past

1.1: Exercise 1: Use would / wouldn't and the verb in brackets
1.3: Exercise 3: Answer these questions using your own ideas

2.3: Exercise 3: Answer these questions with your own ideas

slides.title: Second Conditional
slides.question: What would you do if things were different now?
slides.summary: We use the second conditional for imaginary or unlikely situations in the present or future. The if-clause uses the past simple and the main clause uses would + verb. We often say "were" instead of "was": If I were rich, I would travel.

expressions.meaning: an imaginary situation now: If I had time, I would help.
"were" is common for all people: If she were here…
the imaginary result: I would go. I wouldn't stay.

expressions.en: If I were you, I would…
expressions.meaning: a very common way to give advice.
the question form: would comes before the subject.

items.question: What would you do if you had a million dollars?
blocks: If I had a million dollars,
items.explain: If + past simple (had), then would + verb (would buy).

items.question: If you could live anywhere, where would you live?
items.explain: "Could" is the past of can, so it works in the if-clause.

items.question: If you could meet any famous person, who would you meet?
items.explain: You can join two results with "and": I would meet him and ask him…

items.question: If you had a superpower, what would it be?
items.explain: "It would be…" is a simple way to name your choice.

items.question: If you didn't have to work or study, how would you spend your time?
blocks: If I didn't have to work,
items.explain: Negative if-clause: didn't + verb. Spend time + -ING: spend my time travelling.

slides.title: Third Conditional
slides.question: How would things have been different in the past?
slides.summary: We use the third conditional for imaginary situations in the past: things that didn't happen. The if-clause uses had + past participle and the main clause uses would have + past participle. Use might have or could have when you are less sure.

expressions.meaning: the imaginary past: If I had studied…
the imaginary past result: I would have passed.
a less certain result: I might have passed.

expressions.en: If I hadn't…, I wouldn't have…
expressions.meaning: the negative form: If I hadn't missed the bus…

expressions.en: What would you have done if…?
expressions.meaning: the question form about the past.

items.question: What would you have done if you had won the lottery last year?
blocks: If I had won the lottery,
items.explain: If + had won, then would have + past participle (paid, travelled).

items.question: If you had known English earlier, how would your life have been different?
blocks: If I had learned English earlier,
items.explain: "Would have had" is correct: have + the past participle of have (had).

items.question: If you had met your best friend earlier, how would things have changed?
blocks: If I had met him earlier,
items.explain: Met is the past participle of meet: had met.

items.question: Where would you have gone if you had had more time last summer?
blocks: If I had had more time,
items.explain: "Had had" is normal English: past perfect of have. Gone is the participle of go.

items.question: If you hadn't chosen your current job, what would you have done instead?
blocks: If I hadn't chosen this job,
items.explain: Negative past perfect: hadn't + past participle (chosen).

practice.prompt: If I had more free time, I ___ (learn) another language.
practice.explain: Main clause: would + verb. If + past simple (had).
practice.tip: Great for talking about plans you can't do yet.

practice.prompt: If she were here, she ___ (help) us.
practice.explain: "Were" in the if-clause, would + verb in the result.

practice.prompt: If they lived near the sea, they ___ (go) swimming every day.
practice.explain: Would + verb: would go. "Go swimming" is a fixed expression.

practice.prompt: If I were rich, I ___ (travel) around the world.
practice.explain: Would + base verb, without "to": would travel.

practice.prompt: If he didn't have to work tomorrow, he ___ (come) with us.
practice.explain: Negative if-clause (didn't have to), positive result (would come).

practice.prompt: have more money / go on holiday
practice.explain: If + past simple (had), would + verb (would go).

practice.prompt: be the president / change the law
practice.explain: With "be" we usually say "If I were".

practice.prompt: know French / live in Paris
practice.explain: Knew is the past simple of know.

practice.prompt: be taller / play basketball
practice.explain: If I were + adjective, then would + verb.

practice.prompt: see a ghost / run away
practice.explain: Saw is the past simple of see.

practice.prompt: If I will see him, I would tell him the news.
accept: If I saw him, I would tell him the news.
If I see him, I will tell him the news.
practice.explain: Never use will in the if-clause. Second conditional: If I saw him, I would tell him.
practice.tip: If you mean a real possibility, the first conditional also works: If I see him, I will tell him.

practice.prompt: If she have more time, she would learn Spanish.
accept: If she had more time, she would learn Spanish.
practice.explain: The if-clause needs the past simple: had.

practice.prompt: I would help you if I am free.
accept: I would help you if I were free.
I would help you if I was free.
practice.explain: The if-clause needs the past: were (or was). The if-clause can come second.

practice.prompt: If they lives in Canada, they would speak English every day.
accept: If they lived in Canada, they would speak English every day.
practice.explain: Past simple in the if-clause: lived.

practice.prompt: What you would do if you won the lottery?
accept: What would you do if you won the lottery?
practice.explain: In questions, would comes before the subject: What would you do…?

practice.prompt: If I ___ (study) harder, I ___ (pass) the exam.
practice.explain: If + had + past participle; main clause: would have + past participle.

practice.prompt: If they ___ (leave) earlier, they ___ (catch) the train.
practice.explain: Irregular participles: leave → left, catch → caught.

practice.prompt: If she ___ (know) about the meeting, she ___ (come).
practice.explain: Irregular participles: know → known, come → come.

practice.prompt: If we ___ (book) the tickets in advance, we ___ (get) better seats.
practice.explain: Get → got (British) or gotten (American). Both are correct.

practice.prompt: If he ___ (drive) more carefully, he ___ (avoid) the accident.
practice.explain: Irregular participle: drive → driven.

practice.prompt: not forget my umbrella / not get wet
practice.explain: Negative: hadn't + participle, wouldn't have + participle.

practice.prompt: know about the party / go
practice.explain: Know → known, go → gone.

practice.prompt: study medicine / become a doctor
practice.explain: Become → become (same form).

practice.prompt: set an alarm / wake up on time
practice.explain: Set → set, wake → woken.

practice.prompt: save more money / buy a new phone
practice.explain: Buy → bought.

practice.prompt: If I would have seen her, I would have said hello.
accept: If I had seen her, I would have said hello.
practice.explain: No "would" in the if-clause. Use had + past participle: If I had seen her.

practice.prompt: If they had knew, they would have helped us.
accept: If they had known, they would have helped us.
practice.explain: After had we need the past participle: known, not knew.

practice.prompt: I had come if you had invited me.
accept: I would have come if you had invited me.
practice.explain: The main clause needs would have + past participle.

practice.prompt: If she wouldn't have lost her passport, she wouldn't have missed the flight.
accept: If she hadn't lost her passport, she wouldn't have missed the flight.
practice.explain: No "would" in the if-clause: If she hadn't lost…

practice.prompt: What you would have done if it had rained?
accept: What would you have done if it had rained?
practice.explain: In questions, would comes before the subject: What would you have done…?

practice.prompt: If I ___ you, I would talk to her.
practice.explain: "If I were you" is the fixed form for advice.
practice.tip: At work: "If I were you, I would check the contract again."

practice.prompt: If she ___ the job, she would move to London.
practice.explain: Second conditional: past simple in the if-clause.

practice.prompt: If I would know the answer, I would tell you.
accept: If I knew the answer, I would tell you.
practice.explain: Never would in the if-clause. Know → knew.

practice.prompt: If I had known about the traffic, I ___ earlier.
practice.explain: Past situation → third conditional: would have + past participle.
practice.tip: "If I had known, I would have…" is very common in apologies.

practice.prompt: I wouldn't have missed the meeting if I ___ the email.
practice.explain: If-clause about the past: had + past participle (read).

practice.prompt: Build the sentence: a past regret at work.
practice.explain: Speak → spoken. Get → got.
practice.tip: Useful to talk about past chances.
